title: Eagle - The Mission
text: Apollo 11 launched in July 1969 with astronauts Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins. Armstrong and Aldrin flew the lunar module Eagle to the surface while Collins stayed in orbit aboard the command module Columbia. The mission was the first to land humans on the Moon.

title: Eagle - The Machine
text: The Apollo lunar module Eagle had two stages. The descent stage contained the landing engine, the landing legs and equipment storage. The ascent stage contained the crew compartment and the ascent engine used to leave the Moon. The two stages were separate pieces with different fates.

title: Eagle - The Journey
text: Eagle separated from Columbia in lunar orbit and descended to the Sea of Tranquility, landing on July 20, 1969. Armstrong and Aldrin spent the following hours preparing for the first moonwalk, while Collins continued orbiting the Moon alone.

title: Eagle - The Discoveries
text: During the Apollo 11 moonwalk, Buzz Aldrin deployed the Early Apollo Scientific Experiments Package, or EASEP, and Armstrong and Aldrin gathered lunar surface samples and described them to Mission Control. The returned samples gave scientists their first direct look at lunar material.

title: Eagle - What Remains
text: The Apollo 11 Lunar Module Eagle (1969) carried the first humans to land on the Moon. Its descent stage was intentionally left on the lunar surface after the astronauts returned in the ascent stage. The descent stage and the ascent stage must not be confused: they had different fates.

title: Surveyor 3 - The Mission
text: Surveyor 3 (1967) was an uncrewed robotic lunar lander. It was part of the Surveyor series, which gathered information about the lunar surface to prepare for crewed Apollo landings.

title: Surveyor 3 - The Machine
text: Surveyor 3 was a three-legged lander equipped with a television camera and a surface sampler arm with a scoop. The camera photographed the landing area and the scoop was used to dig into the lunar soil to test its mechanical properties.

title: Surveyor 3 - The Journey
text: Surveyor 3 launched in April 1967 and made a soft landing on the Moon a few days later, in a crater in the Ocean of Storms region. After landing it began transmitting images to Earth.

title: Surveyor 3 - The Discoveries
text: Surveyor 3 returned thousands of images and used its scoop to test the lunar soil. These results helped show that the lunar surface could support a landing spacecraft and its astronauts.

title: Surveyor 3 - What Remains
text: Surveyor 3 (1967) was an uncrewed robotic lunar lander. In 1969, Apollo 12 astronauts visited the lander on the Moon and retrieved several of its parts to bring back to Earth for study.

title: Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle - The Mission
text: Apollo 15 (1971) carried the first Lunar Roving Vehicle, a wheeled rover driven by astronauts on the Moon to expand surface exploration beyond walking distance from the lander.

title: Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle - The Machine
text: The Lunar Roving Vehicle was an electric, four-wheeled vehicle designed to fold up for transport on the lunar module. After landing, the astronauts unfolded it and drove it across the lunar surface.

title: Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle - The Journey
text: Apollo 15 landed near Hadley Rille and the Apennine Mountains in July 1971. Astronauts David Scott and James Irwin used the Lunar Roving Vehicle to explore the area around the landing site over three days of surface activity.

title: Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle - The Discoveries
text: The rover let the Apollo 15 crew travel farther and collect samples from more varied locations than they could on foot. The returned rocks included ancient lunar material that helped scientists study the Moon's formation.

title: Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle - What Remains
text: The Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle (1971) was the first wheeled rover driven by astronauts on the Moon to expand surface exploration. It was left parked on the lunar surface after the mission ended.

title: Sojourner - The Mission
text: Sojourner (1997) was a small robotic rover deployed as part of the Mars Pathfinder mission, marking an early milestone in Martian surface robotics.

title: Sojourner - The Machine
text: Sojourner was a small, solar-powered, six-wheeled rover carried to Mars by the Pathfinder lander. It carried cameras and an instrument for studying the chemical composition of rocks and soil.

title: Sojourner - The Journey
text: Mars Pathfinder reached Mars on July 4, 1997, landing with the help of airbags. Sojourner then drove down a ramp onto the Martian surface and began exploring the area near the lander.

title: Sojourner - The Discoveries
text: Sojourner analyzed rocks and soil near the Pathfinder landing site. Its success demonstrated that a small rover could do useful science on Mars and helped pave the way for later, larger Mars rovers.

title: Sojourner - What Remains
text: Sojourner (1997) was a small robotic rover deployed as part of the Mars Pathfinder mission, marking an early milestone in Martian surface robotics. Final contact occurred in September 1997, and its exact final state and location remain unconfirmed.

title: Spirit - The Mission
text: Spirit was one of two Mars Exploration Rovers that landed on Mars in 2004. It landed in Gusev Crater to look for rocks and soils that could reveal whether the area was once wet.

title: Spirit - The Machine
text: Spirit was a solar-powered, six-wheeled rover equipped with cameras, a robotic arm and scientific instruments for studying rocks and soil, acting as a robotic field geologist.

title: Spirit - The Journey
text: Spirit launched in 2003 and landed on Mars in January 2004. Its primary mission was planned for about three months, but the rover continued operating and driving for years, reaching the Columbia Hills.

title: Spirit - The Discoveries
text: Spirit (2004) made major discoveries regarding Martian rocks and minerals altered by past water, revealing Mars's geological history.

title: Spirit - What Remains
text: NASA's last communication with Spirit was on March 22, 2010, and recovery attempts officially ended on May 25, 2011.

title: Opportunity - The Mission
text: Opportunity was one of two Mars Exploration Rovers that landed on Mars in 2004. It landed on Meridiani Planum to search for evidence that water once existed there.

title: Opportunity - The Machine
text: Opportunity was a twin of the Spirit rover: solar-powered and six-wheeled, with cameras, a robotic arm and instruments for studying rocks and soil. Its primary mission was planned for about three months.

title: Opportunity - The Journey
text: Opportunity (2004) far exceeded its planned lifespan, traveling over 45 kilometers across the Martian surface.

title: Opportunity - The Discoveries
text: Opportunity found evidence that water once affected the rocks at Meridiani Planum, helping show that ancient Mars had wetter conditions than today.

title: Opportunity - What Remains
text: Opportunity (2004) far exceeded its planned lifespan, traveling over 45 kilometers across the Martian surface. Final contact occurred on June 10, 2018 during a global dust storm, and NASA officially declared the mission complete on February 13, 2019.
